question.text: Set-up costs (Organisational Expenses) of an AIF are typically capped at approximately what percentage of total capital commitments, per Chapter 6?

answer.text: Up to 0.25% of commitments, always one-shot
Up to 1.5% to 2.5% of commitments, amortisable over the first 36 months or fund life
Up to 5% of commitments, paid only at fund termination
Up to 10% of NAV per year

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 explicitly caps Set-up / Organisational Costs at 1.5% to 2.5% of total capital commitments, amortisable over 36 months or over fund tenure, from the First Close date. These cover PPM drafting, legal, registration, intermediary fees. The Trap: A understates; C is too high and wrongly timed; D confuses operating expenses with set-up. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this cap. SEBI's AIF Master Circular references disclosure norms on set-up cost allocation. Manager's Pro-Tip: Allocate set-up costs PRO-RATA across investors by committed capital. Investors coming in at later closes should pay their share plus interest (the 'equalisation premium') — specify this explicitly in the PPM to avoid Day-2 disputes.
